question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hear someone out

options.text: Let someone complete what they are saying
Dismiss someone from listening to you

solution:
The correct answer is **"Let someone complete what they are saying".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom** 'Hear someone out' **is '**Let someone complete what they are saying.(बात सुनना)**
 
• This idiom emphasizes the importance of actively listening to someone's perspective or point of view without rushing to judgement or interrupting them.
 
 
• **Example;** John was upset, so I decided to hear him out and understand his perspective before offering any advice.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct idiom is **"let someone complete what they are saying".**

Therefore, the explanation given above, it is clear that the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Hear from far away"**: This idiom does not align with the idiom's common usage.
 
• **"Dismiss someone from listening to you"**: This is the opposite of the intended meaning.
 
• **"Keep someone out"**: This also does not fit the meaning of the idiom.
